experiment: Keep the native 7.5 m grid and change only the exact KFS boundary to the pre-existing all-block accepted candidate nearest 10 km, or the highest all-block accepted candidate when persistence does not reach 10 km. No vertical aggregation and no rerun of Rayleigh QA. Compare to persisted productive method-v4 aerosol backscatter only where the productive retrieval is finite.
interpretation: Moving only the exact boundary on the native grid already changes the lower-column retrieval materially across the campaign.
The boundary-only median and p95 lower-column differences are larger than the same-boundary aggregation experiment, so high-boundary sensitivity is not primarily a vertical-rebinning artifact.

Even cases with complete paths at the higher boundary can show large lower-column differences, demonstrating that path completeness and Rayleigh-window shape QA do not validate the aerosol-free boundary assumption beta_aer(ref)=0.
The two invalid exact-reference runs reproduce the known semantic distinction between window QA and exact-bin KFS usability.
decision: A future high-column method cannot select a higher boundary solely from Rayleigh shape QA, persistence and path completeness. Boundary-condition validity must be addressed explicitly before any method-v5 proposal.
